facts: $\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}} = \dfrac{\Delta d}{\Delta t}$, where $d$ records cumulative distance travelled.
On a distance–time graph where distance records cumulative distance travelled, the gradient of a straight segment is the constant speed during that stage.
A horizontal segment means the object is stopped, and that stopped time still counts in the total time.
The average speed for a whole journey is **not generally** the mean of the leg speeds; it is their arithmetic mean when the legs have equal durations.
For an out-and-back trip, add the distance both ways, because distance travelled is not net displacement.
Speed units are metres per second ($\text{m/s}$) or kilometres per hour ($\text{km/h}$).
steps: Find the total distance travelled over the journey from the graph or description.
Find the total time taken, including all stops and rest periods: $\Delta t = t_{\text{final}} - t_{\text{start}}$.
State the result with the correct speed units.

workedExamples.question_text: A bee flies $96\text{ m}$ in $15\text{ s}$ at constant speed. Find its speed.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The endpoints are $(0,0)$ and $(2,120)$. The line's gradient gives the average speed.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Average speed}&=\dfrac{\Delta d}{\Delta t}\\&=\dfrac{120-0}{2-0}\\&=60\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A runner travels $11\text{ km}$ in $48\text{ minutes}$ at constant speed. Find the speed in $\text{km/h}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert the time to hours.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time}&=\dfrac{48}{60}\\&=0.8\text{ h}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Speed}&=\dfrac{11}{0.8}\\&=13.75\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A drone travels $325\text{ m}$ in $24\text{ s}$ at constant speed. Find its speed in $\text{m/s}$, rounded to $2$ decimal places.
A boat travels $2.85\text{ km}$ in $2\text{ min }30\text{ s}$ at constant speed. Find its speed in $\text{m/s}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert the distance to metres and the whole elapsed time to seconds.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Distance}&=2.85\times1000\\&=2850\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time}&=2\times60+30\\&=150\text{ s}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Speed}&=\dfrac{2850}{150}\\&=19\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$
